visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy delivers a prescription to a patient's home. A toll-free number connects the patient to a pharmacist during the pharmacy's regular hours, but the number appears only on the delivery receipt and not on the prescription container label. The pharmacy's record contains no entry showing that the patient failed to accept an offer to counsel. Which conclusion best separates the two legal issues?

choices.text: The remote-delivery requirement is satisfied by the receipt, and the absent refusal record creates no presumption.
The label placement fails the remote-delivery requirement, but the absent failure-to-accept record creates the statutory presumption that counseling was provided.
The missing label number defeats both remote access compliance and the statutory counseling presumption.
The remote-delivery requirement is satisfied whenever a pharmacist is reachable, but counseling is presumed not to have occurred without an affirmative counseling note.
The statutory presumption applies only if the toll-free number appears on both the receipt and the container label.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy that holds the equipment and the ingredients turns away a request for a simple non-sterile oral suspension that is customary in its community, telling the parent it prefers not to compound. Later the same day it declines a request for a sterile preparation. How should the two refusals be assessed?

choices.text: Both are permitted, since compounding is a service a pharmacy may choose to offer.
Both are prohibited, since a licensee may not refuse to compound on preference.
The first refusal is permitted and the second refusal is prohibited on these facts.
The first refusal is prohibited and the second falls outside the duty entirely.
Both turn on whether another nearby pharmacy could have compounded them instead.

visible.stem: At a busy Massachusetts pharmacy a patient accepts the offer to counsel on a new prescription. The only personnel free are a certified pharmacy technician and a pharmacy intern; the pharmacist is verifying another order. Who may deliver the counseling?

choices.text: The certified pharmacy technician, because certification covers patient communication.
The certified pharmacy technician, provided the pharmacist reviews the encounter afterwards.
Neither of them, because only the pharmacist personally may counsel a patient.
Either of them, because both may relay the pharmacist's offer to counsel.
The pharmacy intern, because counseling shall be made by a pharmacist or a pharmacy intern.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy partially fills a Schedule II prescription at the patient's request two days after the prescription was issued. On day 29 after issuance, the patient asks a different pharmacy to dispense the balance because the first pharmacy is closed. On day 31, the patient returns to the first pharmacy for the balance. Which assessment is correct?

choices.text: The second pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 29 because the federal 30-day period has not expired.
The first pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 31 because the 30 days run from the initial partial fill.

visible.stem: A patient telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy and asks it to bring over a prescription held at another pharmacy. Which statement best describes the receiving pharmacy's position?

choices.text: Both the fee and the requirement that she call the other pharmacy are permissible.
The fee is permissible, but the pharmacy must make the call itself.
The fee is not permissible, and the pharmacy may act as her agent to obtain the transfer.
The fee is not permissible, but the patient must still initiate the transfer herself.
Neither is permissible, because only the transferring pharmacy may charge or initiate.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is launching a monthly in-store injection service for a medication that Massachusetts does not authorize a pharmacist to administer. The written protocol has the pharmacist complete the sale and hand the prefilled syringe to the patient at the register, has the patient carry it to the consultation room and hand it back unopened, and then has the pharmacist give the injection. The protocol assigns the patient no preparation, storage, or handling role, sets no interval between the handover and the return, and runs the same way for every patient. A staff pharmacist asks whether the protocol is acceptable. Which assessment is best?

choices.text: The formal characterization of the handover as a completed dispensing controls, so no administration restriction is engaged.
The patient's possession of the syringe makes the patient rather than the pharmacist the administering party.
The protocol is impermissible, because arranging the steps this way indirectly circumvents the administration restriction.
A valid prescription and a lawful dispensing together authorize the pharmacist to administer the medication.
Responsibility for the arrangement rests with whoever designed the protocol, not with the pharmacist following it.

visible.stem: A neighbour collects a prescription on behalf of a housebound patient. The product is one for which FDA requires a Medication Guide. The pharmacy's practice is to hold the Guide on file and give it to the patient at the next visit, on the view that the Guide belongs to the patient personally. What is the correct assessment of that practice?

choices.text: It is sound, because a Medication Guide must be provided directly to the patient.
It is sound, provided the pharmacy telephones the patient to summarise the Guide.
It is sound only where the collecting person is not a family member.
It is unsound, because the Guide goes to the patient or the patient's agent at the time of dispensing.
It is unsound, because the Guide must be posted to the patient within 24 hours of dispensing.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy makes its offer to counsel by printing a line on the receipt inviting the patient to ask for the pharmacist. Its manager says the statute leaves the method open so long as the patient learns the offer is available. A second patient that day is deaf and cannot use the telephone. What does the statute provide?

choices.text: Any method reaching the patient qualifies, so the receipt line is sufficient.
The offer is made face to face or by telephone, with an alternative where needs require.
The offer must be made face to face in every case, so the telephone is not available.
A printed offer qualifies where the pharmacy also posts a patient rights sign.
The pharmacy may decline to counsel the second patient because of the barrier.

A staff pharmacist asks whether the protocol is acceptable. Which assessment is best?

The patient's possession of the syringe makes the patient rather than the pharmacist the administering party.
The protocol is impermissible, because arranging the steps this way indirectly circumvents the administration restriction.
A valid prescription and a lawful dispensing together authorize the pharmacist to administer the medication.
Responsibility for the arrangement rests with whoever designed the protocol, not with the pharmacist following it.

What is the correct assessment of that practice?

choices.text: It is sound, because a Medication Guide must be provided directly to the patient.
It is sound, provided the pharmacy telephones the patient to summarise the Guide.
It is sound only where the collecting person is not a family member.
It is unsound, because the Guide goes to the patient or the patient's agent at the time of dispensing.
It is unsound, because the Guide must be posted to the patient within 24 hours of dispensing.

choices.text: The formal characterization of the handover as a completed dispensing controls, so no administration restriction is engaged.
The patient's possession of the syringe makes the patient rather than the pharmacist the administering party.
The protocol is impermissible, because arranging the steps this way indirectly circumvents the administration restriction.
A valid prescription and a lawful dispensing together authorize the pharmacist to administer the medication.
Responsibility for the arrangement rests with whoever designed the protocol, not with the pharmacist following it.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician's license has been expired for 26 months. The technician submits the renewal form and fees, but the Board has not renewed the license or decided whether to impose additional conditions. The pharmacy wants the technician to begin work under direct pharmacist supervision. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Submitting the form and fees restores the license provisionally while the Board reviews the application.
Direct pharmacist supervision may permit practice during the renewal review despite the expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years automatically requires a specified national technician examination before renewal.
The technician cannot practice until renewal; because the lapse exceeded two years, additional Board conditions may apply.
A lapse exceeding two years permanently bars renewal of the technician license.

visible.stem:
A noncertified technician with an active Massachusetts license routinely takes filled, pharmacist-verified Schedule II prescriptions to the pickup counter. Today the pharmacist asks the technician to open a stock bottle of methylphenidate tablets and count a new prescription. The pharmacist will perform the final check, and written procedures permit the technician to assist with CII transport.

Which assignment respects the technician’s current scope? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Keep the technician on transport and have the pharmacist count the tablets.
Let the technician count before the pharmacist performs the final check.
Authorize the technician to count by amending the written transport procedure.
Have two ordinary technicians count together and sign the worksheet.

visible.stem:
A Massachusetts technician’s national certification expires on October 12, 2026. The Massachusetts technician license remains active. The technician tells the MOR the same day and plans to seek recertification. The pharmacy has not submitted a report to the Massachusetts Board.

Which steps are required by the cited certification-loss rules? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Keep the certified-technician title during a 14-day reporting grace period.
Report the loss of certification to the Board within 14 calendar days.
Treat the active Massachusetts technician license as automatically revoked.
Defer the Board report until the next Massachusetts technician-license renewal.
Use the pharmacy-technician title and category while certification is lapsed.

visible.stem:
A prescriber telephones a new Schedule VI prescription. The pharmacist on duty approves a Massachusetts-licensed technician with current national certification to receive the call. The prescriber supplies the drug, strength, directions, quantity, and other required information. No therapeutic clarification is needed.

Which workflow is consistent with the technician’s scope? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Route the call to the pharmacist because technician telephone authority is limited to unchanged refills.
Have the technician identify as certified and receive the order for pharmacist review.
Have the technician receive the order and complete its final dispensing verification.
Have the technician complete the clinical review because the prescriber supplied every required field.
